claims: Executed lab scenarios on synthetic data. This is not a HIPAA compliance determination, and NIST SP 800-66 rev2 is guidance, not the regulation.

audit.name: IT GRC lab evidence: NIST SP 800-66 rev2
audit.description: Executed security-lab scenarios on synthetic data, pushed by it-grc. Results are capped at partially_compliant with status in_review and need human review. Not a HIPAA compliance determination.

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-ACCESS Tool authorization (S1, S2, S10)
evidence_groups.description: Allowlisted workload identities call tools within their granted scopes (S1), a tool outside the granted scope is denied (S2) and a granted write succeeds (S10).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-IDENTITY Workload identity (S3, S5, S8)
evidence_groups.description: An unlisted SPIFFE identity is denied (S3), copied pod labels do not impersonate another ServiceAccount (S5) and the gateway calls upstream services with its own identity (S8).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-ASSERTION Assertion authentication (S4, S6, S12, S13)
evidence_groups.description: A cross-resource replay is denied (S4), an untrusted issuer is refused (S6), an expired assertion is refused after SVID renewal (S12) and strict mode rejects a reused assertion (S13).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-FHIR-MTLS FHIR gateway mTLS and OAuth (S15, S16, S17)
evidence_groups.description: The FHIR gateway accepts the allowed SPIRE identity over mutual TLS with OAuth (S15) and refuses a disallowed identity (S16) and a client without a certificate (S17).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-REVOCATION Policy revocation (S9)
evidence_groups.description: New tokens are denied after the grant is removed from the policy (S9).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-KEY-ROTATION Signing key rotation (S11)
evidence_groups.description: After a restart the new signing key is accepted, and a planned overlap keeps tokens signed with the old and the new key verifiable (S11).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-AUDIT-CHAIN Audit hash chain (S14)
evidence_groups.description: Audit record links verify and the checkpoint detects deletion of the log tail (S14).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-FHIR-AUDIT FHIR audit minimization (S18)
evidence_groups.description: FHIR audit records name the calling workload and keep patient ids only as HMAC values (S18).

evidence_groups.name: ITGRC-EV-IDENTITY-LIMITS Identity limits (S7, S10)
evidence_groups.description: In explicit reuse mode a cached SVID is reused within its lifetime (S7), and a valid identity with a granted scope cannot prove the intent of a write (S10).

applied_controls.name: Signing key rotation with overlap
applied_controls.description: Gateway signing keys rotate on restart with a planned overlap, so tokens issued before the rotation stay verifiable (S11). Lab implementation only; production key management is not assessed.

requirements.name: 5. Implement Access Control Procedures Using Selected Hardware and Software
requirements.rationale: Per-tool scopes are enforced for workload identities: allowlisted calls succeed and out-of-scope tools are denied (S1, S2, S10).
requirements.limits: Workload identities and lab tools only; no person users. Sensitive point: identity cannot prove intent (S10), and a cached SVID can be reused within its lifetime (S7).

requirements.name: 2. Implement Policies and Procedures for Authorizing Access
requirements.rationale: Access to lab tools is granted per workload identity and per scope in a policy (S1, S2, S10).
requirements.limits: Workload identities and lab tools only; no documented authorization procedure and no workforce process.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Addressable)
requirements.rationale: Access authorization is enforced per workload identity and per scope (S1, S2, S10).
requirements.limits: Workload identities and lab tools only; no documented authorization procedure and no workforce process.

requirements.name: 3. Ensure that All System Users Have Been Assigned a Unique Identifier
requirements.rationale: Each workload has a unique SPIFFE identity; unlisted or copied identities are refused, and the gateway uses its own identity upstream (S3, S5, S8).
requirements.limits: Workload identities only; unique identifiers for people are not assessed.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Required)
requirements.rationale: Unique workload identification: unlisted or copied identities are refused (S3, S5, S8).
requirements.limits: Workload identities only; unique identifiers for people are not assessed.

requirements.name: 3. Select and Implement   Authentication Options
requirements.rationale: Workload authentication rejects replayed, expired, reused and untrusted assertions, and the FHIR gateway requires an allowed mTLS identity with OAuth (S4, S6, S12, S13, S15 to S17). Key rotation with overlap keeps verification working across restarts (S11).
requirements.limits: Workload authentication in the lab only; person authentication and SMART on FHIR are not implemented. Sensitive point: a cached SVID can be reused within its lifetime (S7), and identity cannot prove intent (S10).

requirements.name: 3. Implement Integrity Controls
requirements.rationale: Calls to the FHIR gateway use mutual TLS with SPIRE certificates; disallowed or missing client certificates are refused (S15 to S17). Key rotation with overlap is supporting evidence (S11).
requirements.limits: Lab SPIRE CA and a sandbox FHIR server only; no transmission inventory, certificate lifecycle or production network.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Addressable)
requirements.rationale: Transmission integrity to the FHIR gateway relies on mutual TLS; disallowed or missing client certificates are refused (S15 to S17).
requirements.limits: Lab SPIRE CA and a sandbox FHIR server only; no transmission inventory, certificate lifecycle or production network.

requirements.name: 4. Implement Encryption
requirements.rationale: Traffic to the FHIR gateway is encrypted with mutual TLS (S15 to S17).
requirements.limits: Lab SPIRE CA and a sandbox FHIR server only; no transmission inventory, certificate lifecycle or production network.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Addressable)
requirements.rationale: Encryption in transit to the FHIR gateway uses mutual TLS (S15 to S17).
requirements.limits: Lab SPIRE CA and a sandbox FHIR server only; no transmission inventory, certificate lifecycle or production network.

requirements.name: 9. Terminate Access if it is No Longer Required
requirements.rationale: Removing a grant from the policy denies new tokens for that workload (S9).
requirements.limits: Tokens issued before a revocation stay valid for up to 300 seconds; workforce termination is not assessed.

requirements.name: 6. Review and Update Access for Users and Processes
requirements.rationale: Access changes in the policy take effect for new token requests (S9).
requirements.limits: Tokens issued before a revocation stay valid for up to 300 seconds; workforce termination is not assessed.

requirements.name: 3. Implement Policies and Procedures for Access Establishment and Modification
requirements.rationale: Access modification is applied through the policy: a removed grant denies new tokens (S9).
requirements.limits: Tokens issued before a revocation stay valid for up to 300 seconds; no documented modification procedure.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Addressable)
requirements.rationale: Access establishment and modification take effect through the policy for new tokens (S9).
requirements.limits: Tokens issued before a revocation stay valid for up to 300 seconds; no documented modification procedure.

requirements.name: 5. Implement the Audit/System Activity Review Process
requirements.rationale: Gateway audit records are hash-chained and a checkpoint detects tail deletion; FHIR audit records name the calling workload (S14, S18).
requirements.limits: Audit records only; the checkpoint is stored beside the log, there is no retention and no regular review process. HMAC patient ids are pseudonymization, not de-identification.

requirements.name: 2. Select the Tools that Will Be Deployed for Auditing and System Activity Reviews
requirements.rationale: A hash-chained audit log with checkpoint verification is the audit tool used in the lab (S14).
requirements.limits: Audit records only; the checkpoint is stored beside the log; no retention and no central collection.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Required)
requirements.rationale: Audit records can be checked for integrity before a review (S14).
requirements.limits: Audit records only; no information system activity review procedure or schedule is evidenced.

requirements.name: 5. Implement a Mechanism to Authenticate ePHI
requirements.rationale: Hash links and the checkpoint detect alteration or deletion of audit records (S14).
requirements.limits: Covers audit records only, not ePHI; the checkpoint is stored beside the log.

requirements.name: Implementation Specification (Addressable)
requirements.rationale: An electronic mechanism detects alteration or deletion of audit records (S14).
requirements.limits: Covers audit records only, not ePHI; the checkpoint is stored beside the log.

requirements.name: 1. Determine the Activities that Will Be Tracked or Audited
requirements.rationale: FHIR access is audited with the calling workload and minimized patient data (S18).
requirements.limits: HMAC patient ids are pseudonymization, not de-identification; the scope is the sandbox FHIR gateway.
